prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
[goal] Incident report for the June game-server outage: window, duration, SLO check, root cause, written to ./result.json.

[action] Read logs/README.md (defines: down = first save error → "server ready"; SLO 99.9%; June = 30 days; one incident). Grepped all three logs for ERROR/FATAL/WARN/ready; read the full incident block in gameserver-2026-06-02.log lines 247-296. Computed the numbers with a short python script and wrote result.json.

[result]
- Start 2026-06-02 03:17:42 (log:251 `ERROR SaveGame failed: ... No space left on device`), end 2026-06-02 03:53:31 (log:294 `INFO server ready, accepting players`).
- minutes_down 35.82 (2149 s exactly, 35 min 49 s).
- availability_june_pct 99.9171: (43200 − 35.8167)/43200 × 100; 99.9% budget is 43.2 min, so slo_999_ok = true.
- root_cause: /data disk filled; save writes failed with ENOSPC, server went unresponsive (watchdog FATAL 03:18:05) and crash-looped with exit code 137 on ~40 restart attempts until `backup rotation freed 38.2 GB on /data` at 03:52:10, then recovered.

Assumptions stated: window per README definition (first save error, not the 03:18:05 FATAL); minutes_down rounded to 2 decimals, availability to 4; timestamps treated as local, same clock throughout; the 06-01 `RCON auth failed` line is unrelated noise, and no other ERROR/FATAL exists in any log, matching the README's "only one incident".

[how I know] Every figure is quoted from grep'd log lines with file and line numbers above; the arithmetic was run in python (output shown: 2149.0 s, 35.8167 min, 99.9170911%, True) and result.json was read back after writing to confirm content.

[next] Nothing blocking; if wanted, I can render this as a markdown postmortem with timeline and action items (disk-space alerting, backup-rotation scheduling).
